The Basilica of Sacré-Cœur in Montmartre, France

With its grand dome and striking white façade, the Basilica of Sacré-Cœur is one of Paris’s best-known landmarks. It sits in Montmartre, the lively neighborhood long associated with artists and painters.

Set atop a 427-foot hill, the basilica offers sweeping views across the city. Designed by Paul Abadie, it was built between 1875 and 1914, rises 272 feet, and was consecrated in 1919.

You can climb to the dome for a panoramic outlook, though the views are less famous than those from the Eiffel Tower or the Arc de Triomphe. The crypt is modest, but the surrounding neighborhood more than makes up for it, with plenty of cafés, restaurants, and shops to explore.

Take the Montmartre funicular to avoid the steep climb and enjoy the area’s artistic atmosphere.

📄 US must demonstrate its adherence to commitments: Iranian MP

📌 Tehran, IRNA — The Islamic Republic will no longer accept an agreement bearing the signature of an American president unless and until the United States demonstrates its adherence to the commitments reached, says Ebrahim Azizi, a lawmaker and the head of the Iranian Parliament’s National Security and Foreign Policy Committee.

In an interview with the Al-Alam news network on Thursday, Azizi addressed a number of regional and international developments, in particular, those related to the Iran–US conflict and the current situation characterized as “neither war nor peace.”
​
Responding to a new proposal from Qatar, necessary guarantees for negotiations, and strategies to counter sanctions, he said that Tehran was evaluating the proposals, but any new agreement would require Washington to fulfil its prior commitments.
​
He further stressed that the era of “worthless signatures” has gone, a reference to non-adherence to and tearing down of deals that were signed with Iran by two US presidents, including incumbent Donald Trump.
​
Referring to the US-Israeli war and the continued rhetoric and pressure campaign, Azizi said Iran is not afraid of anything; rather, it has focused all its efforts on defending its principles, ideals, and values, as well as safeguarding territorial integrity.
​
He noted that the enemy’s hybrid war has been made futile, relying on the measures and guidance of the martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution, as well as the strategies and directives of the current Leader, Ayatollah Sayyid Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei.
​
The Americans had sought to achieve the disintegration, surrender, and overthrow of the Islamic Republic of Iran within three days; however, none of these objectives were realized, and they have now shifted their entire focus toward the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, he added.
​
Regarding Qatar’s new proposal, Azizi stated that Iran has been reviewing proposals, but the criteria of national interests and national security remain intact, no matter which nation mediates between Tehran and Washington.
​
He further said that any nuclear issue cannot be addressed within the framework of the current negotiation process until the United States fulfills its commitments, underscoring that Iran had repeatedly declared its missile and nuclear technology as non-negotiable “red lines.”
​
Emphasizing that Iran does not trust the United States, the lawmaker noted that many other nations in the region and beyond no longer trust Washington because of its policies.
​
Elsewhere, Azizi praised Iraq for expelling US military personnel from the country, advising Iraqi officials not to be deceived by the promises made by the US President and to remain vigilant regarding Washington’s commitments.
​
Referring to a recent quadrilateral meeting between top officials from Turkiye, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan, Azizi interpreted these developments as a sign that regional nations are shifting their perspective on security.
